headline: Chips Drag, Housing Holds Firm as Markets Stumble Into Long Weekend
body_html:
Friday's session ended the week on a sour note, with decliners outpacing advancers by a wide margin — 353 names lower against just 194 higher across the 549-stock universe. The semiconductor group bore the sharpest pain, shedding 3.49% as a group, with Marvell Technology off more than 10%, Semtech down nearly 8%, and both FormFactor and Onto Innovation sliding roughly 7.5%. The rout rippled into industrials, which fell 1.17%, and healthcare, which shed 0.67%.

Against that backdrop, two bright spots stood out. Homebuilders bucked the selloff with a 0.85% advance — the best of any sector — while consumer names edged 0.34% higher, lifted in part by Gap Inc.'s outsized 12.94% surge on what appeared to be strong earnings reception. Solstice Advanced Materials added 12.76%, making specialty chemicals an unlikely pocket of strength. The week's broader earnings theme — that artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending is not a zero-sum competition — may temper some chip-sector anxiety heading into the new week.

Traders return Tuesday with a packed macro calendar and festering geopolitical cross-currents. Treasury Secretary Bessent faces a G20 diplomacy test as tariff tensions, the ongoing Iran conflict, and bond-market volatility all press simultaneously. Fed-watcher focus sharpens on the September meeting after a prominent inflation warning from Fed Governor Warsh. Vietnam's renewed overtures toward US trade talks offer a rare constructive signal amid the noise.

briefs.headline: Bessent Confronts a Crowded G20 Agenda
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent heads into the G20 summit carrying a heavy diplomatic load: tariff disputes, the Iran war's financial fallout, and signs of bond-market stress all demanding attention simultaneously. His ability to project stability while managing adversarial counterparts will be closely watched by fixed-income and currency traders this week.

briefs.headline: Warsh Inflation Warning Puts September Fed Meeting in the Spotlight
briefs.body: A pointed inflation caution from Fed Governor Warsh has raised the stakes for the Federal Reserve's September gathering, setting up what could be the most consequential policy debate of the summer. Markets will parse every data release this week — particularly labor and inflation prints — for clues on the committee's direction.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Selloff Broadens Beyond a Single Name
briefs.body: Friday's chip-sector decline of 3.49% was anything but concentrated. Marvell Technology fell 10.28%, while Semtech, FormFactor, Onto Innovation, and Vicor each dropped between 7.5% and 8%, suggesting sector-wide pressure rather than company-specific news. Investors will watch for any guidance updates or supply-chain commentary in the coming sessions.

briefs.headline: Gulf Tensions Deepen as Khamenei Sends Message to Arab Leaders
briefs.body: Iran's supreme leader dispatched a written appeal to Gulf rulers urging them to unite against what he called a common adversary, escalating the rhetorical front of a conflict already straining regional diplomacy. The message arrives as US military families mark six months of the Iran war, adding to pressure on Washington's foreign-policy bandwidth.

briefs.headline: New Defence Pact Talks Signal Shifting Regional Alignments
briefs.body: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan are set to convene their first formal meeting under a nascent trilateral defence arrangement, according to a source familiar with the talks. The gathering marks a notable realignment among three significant emerging-market economies and could influence energy, currency, and sovereign-debt positioning across the MENA and South Asian regions.

briefs.headline: Yen Volatility Surfaces as Bessent Sounds the Alarm
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly cautioned that disorderly moves in the Japanese yen carry the potential to destabilize global markets — unusually direct language from a senior US official. Currency traders will be alert to intervention signals from Tokyo and any coordinated G20 response language as the week's meetings unfold.
